page: OVHcloud b2-15-flex is a general-purpose cloud instance powered by a KVM hypervisor on the x86_64 architecture. It provides 4 dedicated Intel Haswell cores running at 2.0 GHz without hyperthreading, alongside 15 GB of system RAM, allocating 3.75 GB per core. The instance includes 50 GB of local SSD storage and operates without an attached GPU accelerator.

Benchmark results reflect the older Haswell CPU architecture and moderate clock frequency. In compute testing, the instance achieved a Geekbench single-core score of 845.0 and a multi-core score of 2654.0, while PassMark yielded an overall CPU score of 4915.31. Memory operations demonstrated average throughput on large read transfers at 39.98 GB/sec, though write throughput dropped to 24.28 GB/sec. Redis SET operations reached 4.73 million operations per second, and static web serving throughput reached 3.89 GB/sec.

The primary tradeoff of the b2-15-flex is lower per-core compute performance compared to modern architectures, offset by dedicated core allocation and balanced memory density. With a dedicated four-core execution environment and 15 GB of RAM, it serves non-latency-critical background workers, staging systems, small web servers, and moderate caching or internal tooling tasks that do not require modern vector acceleration or high disk throughput.
description: OVHcloud b2-15-flex is a general-purpose virtual machine offering 4 dedicated Intel Haswell cores at 2.0 GHz and 15 GB of system memory, yielding 3.75 GB per core. Running under a KVM hypervisor on the x86_64 architecture, the configuration includes 50 GB of bundled local SSD storage and operates without discrete GPU acceleration. Synthetic benchmarks reflect the legacy nature of the Haswell CPU generation, scoring 845.0 in Geekbench single-core, 2654.0 in multi-core, and 4915.31 in PassMark CPU tests. Memory read throughput maintains 39.98 GB/sec on uncached blocks, supporting steady data retrieval. While limited in compute-heavy or vector-intensive applications, the balanced 1:3.75 vCPU-to-RAM ratio provides cost-efficient hosting for development environments, small web applications, internal administrative utilities, and low-traffic back-end services.
